article.articleHeadline: Flu not going away? Delhi-NCR reports 1,344 H1N1 cases; doctors reveal warning signs you shouldn't ignore
article.articleSummary: Delhi-NCR reports a sharp surge in H1N1 influenza, with Delhi recording 1,344 cases this season, up from 229 by September last year. Gurgaon and Faridabad hospitals report rising flu-like patients; Paras Health in Gurgaon sees 15–20 such cases over the past two weeks, while Sarvodaya Hospital in Faridabad notes higher risk for older adults and people with diabetes, heart or lung disease, or weakened immunity. Symptoms include fever, cough, sore throat, body aches and fatigue; persistent fever or worsening cough, breathing difficulty or unusual weakness warrant medical evaluation, especially for children. About 1,344 patients diagnosed so far have been treated and discharged; testing is guided by clinical suspicion, not universal screening. Safdarjung Hospital reported 11 confirmed cases in July and five more through Aug 5; PSRI Hospital describes a four-fold surge with some viral pneumonia requiring ICU care. Preventive measures: hand hygiene, vaccination, and consulting a doctor before antivirals. Regions: Delhi, Gurgaon, Noida, Faridabad, Ghaziabad.

triage.headline_ja: インフルエンザは収まらない？デリー首都圏でH1N1症例1,344件を報告、医師が見逃すべきでない警告サインを指摘
triage.triage_reason: デリー首都圏で季節性H1N1症例の増加とICU収容例が報告されているが、既知の流行株であり国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは低いため、続報を注視する。
triage.notes: H1N1は既知の季節性インフルエンザ株であり、前年比で症例数増加とICU収容例（ウイルス性肺炎）が報告されているが、死亡例や国際的拡大の言及はない。今後の重症化・死亡例の動向を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: How Ebola response worker fights fastest-growing outbreak without pay
article.articleSummary: In the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo’s Ituri province, the Ebola outbreak declared mid‑May — centered in Bunia — has become the fastest-growing on record, with confirmed cases surpassing 4,000 and more than 1,800 deaths. The outbreak is linked to the Bundibugyo virus, for which there are no approved vaccines or treatments. Frontline responders, including Wiza Bondele at an Ebola treatment hospital, disinfect contaminated areas, check visitors’ temperatures, and enforce handwashing, while working without pay since the outbreak began. Promised monthly salaries of about $510 have largely not arrived; payments are now routed via mobile money, but delays persist and some workers report partial or no payment. Strikes disrupted care amid armed conflict and deep mistrust. Communities resist prevention measures and burial restrictions, complicating containment; the outbreak is the second-largest on record after 2014–2016 West Africa, with earlier outbreaks (2018–2020) killing at least 2,200.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ対応従事者、報酬なしで史上最速の感染拡大と闘う
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国イトゥリ州で史上最速の拡大を示すエボラ出血熱アウトブレイク（症例4000超、死者1800超）が発生し、ワクチン・治療薬未承認、医療従事者の未払い・ストライキ、地域社会の抵抗により封じ込めが困難となっているため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 発生地域にAngolaが含まれるが、記事サマリーではDRC（イトゥリ州ブニア）のみが主題であり、Angolaでの発生は言及されていないため除外した。Bundibugyoウイルスによるアウトブレイクで承認ワクチン・治療薬が存在しない点、武力紛争下での対応困難、医療従事者への未払いによるストライキなど、管理可能性・拡大リスクが高い状況。

article.articleHeadline: للمرة الأولى منذ تفشي الوباء.. عدد الإصابات بـ"إيبولا" تجاوز الـ4 آلاف
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: For the first time since the outbreak, the number of Ebola infections has surpassed 4,000.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-08-07, Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), caused by the Bundibugyo strain, has reached 4,000 confirmed cases with over 1,800 deaths since the outbreak began in May. This outbreak is described as the fastest-spreading EBOLA in history; case counts are more than eight times higher at this stage than the West Africa 2014 epidemic, and deaths more than six times higher. Africa CDC and the World Health Organization (WHO) are launching a joint investigation to assess whether the virus has mutated amid rapid transmission, following briefings in Kinshasa. About three months into the outbreak, new infections have doubled in some of the hardest-hit areas. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus highlighted the extraordinary pace and ongoing containment challenges during a visit that occurred amid a health-worker strike.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ流行開始以来初めて、感染者数が4000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ出血熱（ブンディブジョ株）流行が史上最速のペースで拡大し、感染者4000人・死者1800人超に達しており、WHOとAfrica CDCが変異の可能性を含む合同調査を開始するなど国際的関心が極めて高い。
triage.notes: 医療従事者のストライキが対応を妨げている点、変異の可能性を含む調査が進行中である点はフルRRAで重点的に確認すべき。

article.articleHeadline: ‎ ‎وفاة 13 وإصابة 240 بالكوليرا في تشاد منذ إعلان تفشي العدوى‎ ‎
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 13 dead and 240 infected with cholera in Chad since the outbreak was announced.
article.articleSummary: Chad reports a cholera outbreak with 240 infections and 13 deaths since it was officially announced in late July (case fatality about 5.4%). By the prior Monday, 239 cases and 13 fatalities had been recorded, most in the Hadjer-Lamis region in the north and in Ndjamena, where 11 deaths occurred in August, indicating rapid spread in dense urban areas. First outbreak deaths were on June 13. Limited access to safe drinking water and sanitation remains a key driver, despite some improvements in water systems elsewhere. About 50,800 people have received cholera vaccines since July 24 as part of a targeted campaign. Cholera is a bacterial disease transmitted via contaminated water or food and is easily treated with early diagnosis, but can be fatal without timely care. Other African countries—Central African Republic, Democratic Republic of Congo, and Nigeria—also face cholera outbreaks amid similar water/sanitation challenges.

triage.headline_ja: チャドでコレラの流行が発表されて以降、13人死亡、240人感染
triage.triage_reason: チャドで死者13人・感染240人（致死率約5.4%）のコレラ流行が都市部で急速に拡大しており、周辺国（中央アフリカ共和国、コンゴ民主共和国、ナイジェリア）でも同様の流行が確認されているため、地域的拡大のリスクがある。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はチャドのコレラ流行だが、チャドは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。記事内で明示的に『コンゴ民主共和国でも同様のコレラ流行が発生している』と述べられているため、DRCのみ対象国として記載。中央アフリカ共和国・ナイジェリアは対象国リスト外。

article.articleHeadline: Pasca Kasus Gigitan Anjing Liar di Padang Batung HSS, Distan PP Segera Laksanakan Vaksinasi Rabies
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Following a stray dog bite case in Padang Batung HSS, Distan PP will promptly carry out rabies vaccination.
article.articleSummary: Rabies risk rising in Padang Batung District, Hulu Sungai Selatan, South Kalimantan, after three dog attacks. Two bite incidents tested positive for rabies at the Balai Veteriner laboratory; a third case remains unconfirmed as the attacking dog has not been located. In response, the Dinas Pertanian, Perikanan, dan Pangan (Distan PP) through the Livestock and Plantations Division will conduct mass rabies vaccination (VAR) for stray and at‑risk dogs across all Padang Batung villages. The program will be preceded by socialization and coordinated with the Camat Padang Batung and village authorities. The aim is proactive prevention rather than treatment after cases, with timing awaiting district instructions. Earlier incidents occurred in Pandulungan, with attacks also reported in Pahampangan and Batu Bini. Three residents received medical care at Puskesmas and the ER of RSUD Brigjend Hasan Basry Kandangan.

triage.headline_ja: パダン・バトゥンHSSでの野犬咬傷事件を受け、Distan PPが狂犬病ワクチン接種を早急に実施
triage.triage_reason: 南カリマンタンの一地域で犬の狂犬病発生と予防的ワクチン接種の動きがあるが、ヒトへの感染事例は確認されておらず、規模も限定的であるため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 地元当局（Distan PP）が野犬への集団ワクチン接種を計画中。3名が咬傷で医療機関を受診したが、ヒトの狂犬病発症例は報告されていない。地域限定の動物由来感染症事例。

article.articleHeadline: Dịch Ebola: Châu Phi triển khai vaccine và mở rộng điều trị
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak: Africa rolls out vaccines and expands treatment.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) worsens as Africa CDC (ACDC) on August 6 expands vaccination with the Ebola Zaire vaccine in Ituri and North Kivu to reduce mortality amid the Bundibugyo driven surge. Vaccinated individuals can still contract Ebola, but no deaths have been recorded among them. ACDC also expands remdesivir use for treatment, drawing on Uganda’s experience where mortality was about 10 percent and the outbreak ended in mid July after the last patient discharge. The DRC Health Ministry tallies 4,053 cases and 1,850 deaths; 793 recovered and 694 still in treatment or isolation. MSF warns the outbreak is spreading rapidly, with 60 to 70 percent of new cases outside monitored lists, expanding to 51 health zones from 9. Kinshasa has reported no confirmed cases, though about 200 passengers on a near Kinshasa ship were quarantined after a traveler died with suspected Ebola symptoms. Eleven other African countries are at high risk: South Sudan, Rwanda, Kenya, Zambia, Central African Republic, Tanzania, Ethiopia, Angola, Republic of Congo, Burundi, Somalia.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ流行:アフリカでワクチン展開と治療拡大
triage.triage_reason: DRCでエボラ流行が拡大し(4,053症例、1,850死亡、致死率約45%)、51保健地域に拡大、複数国が高リスクとされており、国際的拡大リスクと重大な公衆衛生影響が認められるため。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCでのエボラ流行拡大を主題とし、ザンビアを含む11カ国が高リスク国として言及されているが、感染確認例はDRCのみ。ザンビアは高リスク国として明示的に列挙されているためverified_locationsに含めた。他の高リスク国（南スーダン、ルワンダ等）は対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: الكونغو الديمقراطية: ارتفاع عدد إصابات إيبولا إلى أكثر من 4 آلاف حالة للمرة الأولى منذ تفشي الوباء
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Democratic Republic of the Congo: Ebola infections rise to more than 4,000 cases for the first time since the outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Laboratory-confirmed Ebola infections in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have surpassed 4,000 for the first time since the outbreak, with 4,053 confirmed cases and 1,850 deaths reported as of Friday, 7 August 2026. The current outbreak, centered in eastern provinces, is linked to a Bundibugyo lineage of Ebola and poses major challenges due to weak health infrastructure, population displacement, and insecurity that hinder containment efforts. Ebola virus disease spreads through close contact and contaminated body fluids and causes hemorrhagic fever. The World Health Organization notes this Bundibugyo-linked outbreak lacks a licensed vaccine or approved treatment specific to this strain. By comparison, the 2018–2020 outbreak was the deadliest to date, with about 3,500 cases and roughly 2,300 deaths. Health authorities continue surveillance and response amid a prolonged, difficult fight in eastern DRC.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国：エボラ出血熱感染者数、流行開始以来初めて4000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: 致死率の高いエボラ出血熱がコンゴ民主共和国で4,000例超・死者1,850人に達し、ワクチン・治療薬未承認の株であること、治安不安定・保健インフラ脆弱で封じ込めが困難な点からIHR基準複数該当及び国際支援の必要性が高い。
triage.notes: Bundibugyo系統のエボラで承認済みワクチン・治療薬がなく、治安不安・住民移動により封じ込めが困難。2018-2020年流行を上回る規模となっており、フルRRAでの詳細評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Crise migratoire à Ceuta, Hervé Renard sélectionneur de la Côte d'Ivoire, Ebola : l'hebdo Afrique
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Migration crisis in Ceuta, Hervé Renard, Ivory Coast head coach, Ebola: Africa Weekly
article.articleSummary: Emerging Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo dominates this Africa Weekly briefing. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus urged intensified action after a visit to the Congolese president, as the country reports 3,973 laboratory-confirmed Ebola cases and 1,800 deaths since the outbreak began, underscoring ongoing transmission and the need for stronger public health coordination. The report also notes other headline items, including the Ceuta migrant situation: the Spanish enclave in Morocco saw more than 70,000 arrivals in 24 hours, with at least 79 deaths reported by authorities, while the Moroccan rights group AMDH cites 130 deaths from the crisis. Additional items mention Nigeria's release of 308 kidnapped victims and other regional developments.

triage.headline_ja: セウタの移民危機、コートジボワール代表監督エルベ・ルナール、エボラ出血熱：アフリカ週報
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で検査確認3,973例・死者1,800人という大規模なエボラ出血熱の流行が継続しており、WHO事務局長が現地訪問し対策強化を要請するなど公衆衛生上の深刻な影響と国際的関心が認められるため。
triage.notes: 記事はアフリカ週報の総括記事であり、セウタ移民危機・ナイジェリアの誘拐被害者解放等の話題も含むが、対象国リストに該当するのはDRCのエボラ出血熱のみ。

article.articleHeadline: Bilanțul cazurilor de infectare cu Ebola din RD Congo depășește pragul de 4.000
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola infection case count in DR Congo surpasses the 4,000 mark.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 4,000 confirmed cases in the current outbreak, with 4,053 infections and 1,850 deaths reported by the national public health institute. Five provinces are affected: Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, and Tshopo. Scientists published in Science last month concluded the outbreak began in January or earlier, in Ituri, with more than 500 suspected cases identified between mid-January and May 15. Officials warn that late detection, overwhelmed surveillance, ongoing conflict, and a lack of vaccines and treatments for the Bundibugyo strain have allowed wider spread. The outbreak ranks second in size; only the West Africa epidemic of 2014–2016 exceeded it, with over 28,000 cases in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone. This accounting reflects government data, reported via Reuters.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ感染者数が4,000人の大台を突破
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で進行中のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクが4,000症例・1,850死亡に達し、史上2番目の規模に達している。IHR基準の複数項目に該当し、国際的関心も高い重大事案。
triage.notes: リベリア・ギニア・シエラレオネは2014-2016年の過去の西アフリカアウトブレイクとの比較として言及されているのみで、現在の発生国ではないためverified_locationsから除外した。致死率は約45.6%（1850/4053）と非常に高く、ワクチン・治療薬が不足するBundibugyo株による流行で、紛争地域における監視体制の課題も報告されている。

article.articleHeadline: Congo's Ebola outbreak surpasses 4,000 cases
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in Congo surpasses 4,000 cases, reaching 4,053 infections and 1,850 deaths as of 2026-08-07. The outbreak spans five provinces: Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, and Tshopo, and is described as the fastest-spreading on record and the world's second-largest Ebola epidemic. The public health institute notes infections had been circulating for months before the May 15 declaration. A Science journal report indicates the outbreak began in January or earlier, with more than 500 suspected cases between mid-January and May 15. Contributing factors include delayed detection, overwhelmed surveillance, ongoing military conflict, and a lack of vaccines and treatments for the virus species involved. By comparison, West Africa's 2014-16 outbreak exceeded 28,000 cases across Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ出血熱流行、感染者数が4,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: コンゴでエボラ出血熱の症例数が4,000人を超え、死亡者数も1,850人に達しており、深刻な公衆衛生上の影響と国際的拡大リスクが認められるためフルRRAへ進むべき事案。
triage.notes: 西アフリカの2014-16年流行との比較のためシエラレオネ・リベリア・ギニアが発生地域に含まれるが、これらは過去の事例への言及であり現在の発生国ではないため除外した。

article.articleHeadline: Συναγερμός για τον Έμπολα στο Κονγκό: Πάνω από 4.000 τα επιβεβαιωμένα κρούσματα
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Alarm over Ebola in Congo: More than 4,000 confirmed cases.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has reached more than 4,000 confirmed cases, with official figures at 4,053 cases and 1,850 deaths. The country faces the second-largest and fastest-spreading outbreak on record. Scientists say infections began months before the outbreak was declared on May 15, with Ituri and adjacent provinces bearing the earliest transmission; the latest report lists cases across Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele and Tshopo. A Science journal assessment published last month concluded the outbreak likely started in January or earlier in Ituri, with more than 500 suspected cases identified before May 15. Contributing factors include delayed detection, overwhelmed surveillance, ongoing armed conflict, and a shortage of vaccines and therapies for this outbreak’s Ebola strain, hampering containment. By comparison, West Africa’s 2014–16 outbreak exceeded 28,000 cases across Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラ警戒:確定症例4,000人超
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準のうち深刻な公衆衛生影響・異常性・国際拡大リスクの複数が該当し、致死率の高い大規模エボラ流行が継続中であるためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: Sierra Leone、Angola、Liberia、Guineaは2014-16年の過去の流行との比較で言及されているのみで、現行アウトブレイクの発生国ではないため除外。致死率約45.6%(1850/4053)と極めて高く、武力紛争地域での監視体制の弱さやワクチン・治療薬不足が拡大要因として指摘されている。

article.articleHeadline: Počet obetí eboly v Kongu stúpol na 1850, choroba sa rýchlo šíri
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola death toll in Congo has risen to 1,850; the disease is spreading rapidly.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-08-07, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has 1,850 deaths among 4,053 confirmed cases. Declared May 15, the epidemic has spread from Ituri into North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, and Tshopo, and crossed into neighboring Uganda. The current outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain, for which no licensed vaccine or approved therapy exists. Response is hindered by delays in contact tracing, limited access to affected areas, local distrust, and violence by armed groups and some residents. The outbreak is accelerating faster than the 2014–2016 epidemic (≈28,000 cases, >11,000 deaths), taking longer to reach certain milestones (e.g., 1,000 deaths). Ebola transmits via contact with infected individuals or contaminated materials and presents with fever, vomiting, diarrhea, muscle pains, and bleeding.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ死者数が1,850人に上昇、病気は急速に拡大している
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRC複数州からウガンダへ越境拡大し、死者数・症例数が急増、ワクチン・治療法未承認という重大な公衆衛生上の脅威であり、IHR基準を複数満たすためフルRRAへ進むべきである。
triage.notes: ウガンダへの越境が言及されているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めていない。

article.articleHeadline: Κονγκό: Τα επιβεβαιωμένα κρούσματα Έμπολα ξεπέρασαν τα 4.000
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Congo: The confirmed Ebola cases surpassed 4,000.
article.articleSummary: Confirmed Ebola virus disease cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have risen to over 4,000 for the first time in the current outbreak, reaching 4,053 cases and 1,850 deaths as reported by the public health institute. Five provinces have reported infections: Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele (Upper Uele), and Tshopo. The outbreak is described as the second-largest globally and the fastest-spreading on record. Experts believe infections began months before the May 15 official declaration of an epidemic, with more than 500 suspected cases identified from January to May 15 in Ituri. Contributing factors hindering containment include delays in detection, heightened surveillance burdens, ongoing military conflict, and a lack of vaccines and treatments for the strain. Only the West Africa 2014-16 outbreak was larger (>28,000).

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ：エボラ確定症例数が4,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRCのエボラ流行が確定症例4,000人・死者1,850人を超え、史上2番目の規模かつ最速拡大とされ、紛争やワクチン不足により制御が困難な状況であるため、フルリスク評価が必要と判断される。
triage.notes: Bluedotの発生地域にAngolaが含まれるが、記事サマリーでは言及がなく、DRC国内（Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, Tshopo）のみが確認されているため除外した。

article.articleHeadline: പ്ര​ള​യ​ശേ​ഷം - രോ​ഗ​സാ​ധ്യ​ത​ക​ളും മു​ൻ​ക​രു​ത​ലു​ക​ളും -1 ജ​ല​ജ​ന്യ​രോ​ഗ​ങ്ങ​ൾക്കെതിരേ ജാഗ്രത | Deepika | The Largest Read Malayalam Internet Daily | Online News
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In the aftermath of floods: disease risks and precautions; vigilance against waterborne diseases
article.articleSummary: Post-flood Kerala warns of waterborne diseases including diarrhea, cholera, typhoid, and malaria in flood-affected areas. Public health guidance from the Kerala Health Department emphasizes precautions to prevent transmission. Key measures: drink only boiled water; use bleaching powder for chlorination with dosages of 0.5 g per 20 L, 12.5 g per 500 L, or 25 g per 1000 L, and wait about 30 minutes before consumption. For liquid chlorine, add 20 mL per 1000 L and double the amount for super chlorination, again after about 30 minutes. Use chlorinated water to wash pots, utensils, and vegetables. Wash hands with soap and water before cooking, before eating, and after defecation or vomiting. Well water purification details are provided, along with  chlorine-based dosing guidance. Information credited to State Health and Family Welfare Department, Health Kerala & Kerala Health Services.

triage.headline_ja: 洪水後：疾病リスクと予防策 その1 水系感染症への警戒
triage.triage_reason: 洪水後の水系感染症予防に関する一般的な公衆衛生ガイダンス記事であり、具体的な患者数やアウトブレイクの発生は報告されていない。
triage.notes: 記事はケララ州保健当局による洪水後の予防ガイダンスであり、具体的な症例数やアウトブレイクの確認情報は含まれていない。季節的・定例的な注意喚起の可能性が高い。

article.articleHeadline: Over 17,000 bats documented in JAS
article.articleSummary: DENR-Davao Region documented over 17,000 island flying foxes (Pteropus hypomelanus) and large flying foxes (Pteropus vampyrus) in Jose Abad Santos, Davao Occidental, during the 2026 Monitoring of Threatened Species conducted in Barangay Bukid on Aug 4, 2026. Using the exit count method, observers estimated populations and roost locations by tallying bats as they emerged at dusk for about 30 minutes. Beyond Jose Abad Santos, large flying foxes are also found on Luban Island, Mount Hamiguitan Range Wildlife Sanctuary, and Mount Apo Natural Park. Flying foxes, protected under Republic Act No. 9147, play key ecological roles as pollinators, seed dispersers, and natural pest controllers, yet remain threatened and are recognized natural reservoirs for Nipah virus. The island flying fox is the smallest member of the group, typically roosting on offshore islands in coconut palms and tall trees. The Philippines hosts about 70 bat species, among ~1,400 worldwide.

triage.headline_ja: JAS(ホセ・アバド・サントス)で17,000匹以上のコウモリを記録
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はDENRによるオオコウモリ類の生態調査報告であり、ニパウイルス感染事例やヒトへの感染兆候の報告は一切ない。単に自然保護区でのコウモリ個体数調査結果を伝えるもの。
triage.notes: ニパウイルスの自然宿主であるオオコウモリの生息調査記事であり、実際の感染症発生事例ではないため対象国としては計上しない。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola death toll tops 1.800 in DRC
article.articleSummary: Ebola death toll tops 1,800 in the Democratic Republic of Congo as the outbreak continues to spread rapidly. Africa's top health agency announced on Thursday a rollout of a vaccine targeting a previous Ebola strain in an effort to contain the latest transmission. Nearly three months into the outbreak, global health officials warn the virus is spreading faster than the response, with new cases doubling in some hotspots. Frontline health workers have gone on strike, citing months of unpaid wages. The situation highlights challenges in outbreak control, including workforce shortages and vaccine strategy adjustments amid evolving Ebola strains. The report underscores ongoing transmission within DRC and the urgency of expanded vaccination and public health measures to curb further spread.

triage.headline_ja: DRCでエボラ死者数が1,800人を超える
triage.triage_reason: エボラの死者数が1,800人を超え急速に拡大しており、公衆衛生への深刻な影響と国際的拡大リスクが認められるためフルRRAへ移行すべき。
triage.notes: 医療従事者のストライキや賃金未払い、ワクチン戦略の調整など、対応能力の限界を示す要素が複数あり、国際支援の必要性が高いと考えられる。

article.articleHeadline: Число случаев заражения Эболой в ДРК превысило 4 тысячи
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The number of Ebola cases in the DRC has surpassed 4,000.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-08-07, the Democratic Republic of Congo has confirmed 4,053 Ebola virus disease cases, with 1,850 deaths among the infected. Government statistics cited by Reuters indicate the outbreak continues to spread, making it the second-largest Ebola epidemic globally and one of the fastest-growing in history. The rising tally highlights ongoing transmission within the country and persistent public health challenges in containing the outbreak. The report provides no additional details on geographic distribution, laboratory confirmation, or infection sources in this article. These figures reflect the latest official release and underscore the severity and scale of the current Ebola outbreak in the DRC.

triage.headline_ja: DRCでのエボラ感染者数が4000人を突破
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRCで4,053例・死亡1,850人に達し、史上最速級の大規模流行として拡大が継続しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへの移行が必要。
triage.notes: 致死率は約45.6%と高く、感染拡大が継続中。地理的分布や感染源についての詳細情報は記事に記載がないため不明。

article.articleHeadline: Monkayo under heightened alert due to ASF
article.articleSummary: Monkayo, a municipality in Davao de Oro, Philippines, is under heightened alert due to an alleged African Swine Fever (ASF) outbreak. Executive Order 2026-078 urges hog raisers, swine businesses, and the public to enforce strict biosecurity, avoid transporting unauthorized live swine and pork products, and report sick or dead swine to the Office of the Municipal Agriculturist. ASF is a highly contagious viral disease of domestic pigs and wild boar with case fatality up to 100%. The Philippines’ ASF outbreak began in July 2019; as of July 10, 2026, active ASF cases were recorded in 21 barangays across 17 cities/municipalities in 11 provinces. In support, Davao de Oro inaugurated a P10-million Swine Multiplier and Technology Demonstration Farm under the INSPIRE Program to rehabilitate the hog industry after ASF. Earlier data: by March 24, 2021, 47,401 pigs culled and 10,078 farmers in 209 barangays across 40 LGUs affected in the Davao Region.

triage.headline_ja: モンカヨ、ASF発生によりアラート引き上げ
triage.triage_reason: 動物のみが対象で人への感染症ではないが、フィリピンで継続中のASF拡大状況を示す情報であり経過観察が妥当。
triage.notes: ASFは豚のみに感染する動物疾病でヒトへの感染性はないが、フィリピンの畜産業・貿易への影響として継続監視の価値がある。

article.articleHeadline: लम्पी स्किन रोग पर अलर्ट, बिजनौर प्रशासन ने कसी कमर
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Lumpy Skin Disease Alert: Bijnor Administration Steps Up Measures.
article.articleSummary: Lumpy Skin Disease (LSD) alert in Bijnor district, Uttar Pradesh, with an immediate ban on interstate cattle transport and suspension of cattle markets and fairs until further orders. District Magistrate Jasjit Kaur notes LSD cases in neighboring Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, and parts of western Uttar Pradesh, prompting heightened vigilance in this border district. LSD is a viral disease transmitted by vectors such as mosquitoes and other insects. A district-wide surveillance drive is to be conducted by the Chief Veterinary Officer; any suspected or infected animals will trigger containment, ring vaccination, and other control measures. Under the National Gokul Mission, entry of cattle from other states requires a valid vaccination certificate uploaded to the India Pashudhan app, with verification of the farmer’s Aadhaar number and the animals’ ear tagging. Orders are effective immediately.

triage.headline_ja: ランピースキン病警戒、ビジュノール行政が対策強化
triage.triage_reason: ランピースキン病(LSD)はウシ科動物のみに感染するウイルス性疾患で人獣共通感染症ではなく、人の公衆衛生への直接的影響は認められないため見送りとする。
triage.notes: LSDはウシ・水牛のみに感染し人には感染しない動物疾病。家畜産業への経済的影響はあるが、人の感染症危機管理・バイオセキュリティの観点からは対象外。地方行政による家畜移動制限・監視強化が実施されている段階。

article.articleHeadline: Kasus Ebola di Kongo Tembus 4.000, Korban Jiwa Capai 1.850
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola cases in Congo surpass 4,000, death toll reaches 1,850.
article.articleSummary: As of 7 August 2026, Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 4,000 confirmed cases with 1,850 deaths. Total cases reach 4,053 across five provinces: Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, and Tshopo, according to the Kongo Public Health Institute. Officials say transmission likely began months before the official outbreak declaration on 15 May, with a Science journal report noting more than 500 suspected cases from mid-January to 15 May. Rapid spread is driven by delayed detection, overwhelmed surveillance, armed conflict, and limited vaccines and treatments for the strain involved. Although severe, this outbreak is smaller than West Africa’s 2014–2016 Ebola epidemic. Strengthening early detection, case tracing, treatment access, and vaccine availability is crucial to curb further transmission across the affected regions.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ症例が4,000人を突破、死者数は1,850人に達する
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRCの5州に拡大し4,000症例・1,850死亡と重大な公衆衛生上の影響があり、武力紛争や医療資源不足でヒト-ヒト感染拡大リスクが高いためフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: 発生地域にAngolaが含まれるが、記事サマリーはDRC国内5州（Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, Tshopo）での発生のみを述べており、Angolaへの拡大については言及がないため除外した。

article.articleHeadline: Gujarat's Chandipura virus deaths revive memories of Telangana's 2003 outbreak
article.articleSummary: Chandipura virus (CHPV) resurfaces in Gujarat, causing 22 child deaths (ages 9 months–14 years), reviving memories of the 2003 outbreak in the undivided Warangal, Karimnagar and Khammam districts that killed nearly 200 children. CHPV is a highly pathogenic rhabdovirus transmitted by sandflies (Phlebotomus), causes Acute Encephalitis Syndrome and is not human-to-human contagious. The virus can progress rapidly, with brain involvement within 24–48 hours of infection, presenting as seizures, altered behavior, excessive drowsiness, and rapid progression to coma. There is no licensed antiviral therapy or vaccine; management is supportive, focusing on fever control, seizure management, electrolyte balance, and respiratory support. Early hospitalization offers the best chance of survival. CHPV outbreaks typically surface during the monsoon (May–September) in damp, humid areas near animal shelters.

triage.headline_ja: グジャラート州でのチャンディプラウイルス感染死、テランガナ州2003年アウトブレイクの記憶を呼び起こす
triage.triage_reason: グジャラート州で子供22人が死亡するチャンディプラウイルス感染症が発生し、致死率が高く、ワクチン・治療法がない重篤な疾患であるため、IHR基準を2つ以上満たす。
triage.notes: 記事は2026年現在グジャラート州で発生中のチャンディプラウイルス感染症(22人の子供死亡)を報じており、2003年のテランガナ州(旧ワランガル・カリムナガル・カムマム地区)での約200人死亡のアウトブレイクを歴史的比較として言及している。現在の発生地はグジャラート州のみであり、テランガナ州は過去の事例として言及されているため、verified_locationsはインドのみとした。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola's silent Victims: Why children are dying in large numbers
article.articleSummary: Ebola's Bundibugyo outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo's Ituri Province has surpassed 4,000 confirmed cases, marking the largest epidemic there and the second-largest globally. By August 2, UNICEF counts 743 infections among children aged 0–17, with 330 child deaths; children comprise about a quarter of infections but nearly one-third of deaths. Fear and service disruptions are deterring care, with Mongbwalu General Hospital visits dropping from about 500 per month to near zero. Across Ituri's hotspot zones (Bunia, Mongbwalu, Nizi, Rwampara), essential health service use fell 42% from April–June; across Ituri, primary care declined ~13%. Routine immunisation is hardest hit: first-dose measles vaccinations in Mongbwalu down 69%; third-dose pentavalent down 22%; second-dose measles down 18%, with more than 23,000 fewer routine doses since April. Maternal care also declined: facility deliveries −13% in Ituri overall, with Bunia −38%, Rwampara −30%, Nizi −70%. The article cites the 2014–2016 West Africa Ebola epidemic as historical context.

triage.headline_ja: エボラの静かな犠牲者：なぜ子どもたちが大量に死亡しているのか
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国イトゥリ州のエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）流行が4000例を超え史上2番目の規模となり、子供の死亡が急増、医療サービス利用の大幅低下も報告されており深刻な公衆衛生上の影響が認められる。
triage.notes: 発生地域にRwanda、Angolaが含まれているが、記事サマリーではDRCイトゥリ州のみが主題であり、他国への感染拡大は言及されていないため除外した。既存の大規模アウトブレイクの継続・悪化を示す続報記事であり、子供の死亡率上昇やルーチン医療（麻疹ワクチン接種等）の崩壊が新たな懸念点として強調されている。

article.articleHeadline: Le virus Ebola continue de se propager
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola virus continues to spread.
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo strain of Ebola is spreading in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with transmission now reaching internally displaced person camps in Ituri. Nineteen displaced individuals are infected, five of whom have died. At least five of 69 IDP sites in Ituri have confirmed Ebola cases, with several deaths reported. Approximately 2,000 deaths have occurred from this viral strain overall. UNHCR warns that overcrowding, water and sanitation deficits, and distrust of health services create conditions for rapid spread, while misinformation hinders early detection and safe burials. As of today, 3,973 laboratory-confirmed cases and more than 1,801 deaths have been recorded across Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele and Tshopo; Ituri alone accounts for about 87% of infections. The situation threatens millions of displaced people and calls for strengthened response measures.

triage.headline_ja: エボラウイルスの感染が拡大を続けている
triage.triage_reason: DRCで進行中のエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）流行が国内避難民キャンプにまで拡大し、致死率・症例数ともに深刻化しており、IHR基準複数該当かつ国際支援の必要性が示唆されているため、フルリスク評価が必要と判断。
triage.notes: 既存のDRCエボラ流行（ブンディブギョ株）の拡大継続を報じる記事。IDPキャンプへの感染拡大、UNHCRによる警告、累計3,973例・1,801人以上の死亡が確認されており、既に大規模アウトブレイクとして継続的な監視・支援が必要な事案。

article.articleHeadline: कांगो में इबोला का कहर! 4,053 संक्रमित, 1,850 की मौत; बच्चों पर सबसे ज्यादा मार
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola ravages Congo! 4,053 infected, 1,850 dead; children bear the brunt.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, centered in eastern regions including Ituri. As of 2026-08-07, 4,053 laboratory-confirmed Ebola infections and 1,850 deaths have been recorded. Currently 694 patients are in isolation or hospital, with 793 recoveries. UNICEF reports 330 child deaths, indicating children comprise about a quarter of confirmed cases but roughly a third of fatalities; under-5s are the most affected. The surge has disrupted essential health services such as vaccination and maternal care, with fear and health-facility closures hindering care for malaria, diarrhea, and other treatable diseases. Médecins Sans Frontières warns the outbreak is unfolding at unprecedented speed in eastern DRC, with no signs of slowing. Doctors Without Borders cites bed shortages and overburdened staff contributing to delays in care as communities remain wary.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラが猛威！感染4,053人、死亡1,850人；子どもが最も深刻な被害を受ける
triage.triage_reason: DRC東部でのエボラ流行が4,053例・1,850死亡という大規模かつ急速な拡大を示しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当し、国際支援の必要性も明確なためフルRRAへ進めるべき。
triage.notes: Ituriは対象国リストにないためDRCのみを記載。MSF/UNICEFの報告から医療体制の逼迫と子どもへの深刻な影響が確認されている。

article.articleHeadline: 中國多種病毒齊發 新冠陽性率連續數周居首（視頻） | 新冠疫情 | 哨點醫院 | 流感病毒
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: China Faces Simultaneous Outbreaks of Multiple Viruses; COVID-19 Positivity Rate Tops for Several Consecutive Weeks (Video) | COVID-19 Pandemic | Sentinel Hospital | Influenza Virus
article.articleSummary: China faces simultaneous outbreaks of SARS-CoV-2, influenza, and enteroviruses, with COVID-19 positivity leading in sentinel hospital influenza-like illness samples at 22.3% in week 31 (Jul 27–Aug 2), up 1.9 points; influenza at 13.3%, enteroviruses 4.1%. Among hospitalized severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) cases, COVID-19 positivity is 8.2%, influenza 5.8%, and human metapneumovirus 5.5% (month-to-month increase 1.3 pp for HMPV). The prevailing Omicron NB.1.8.1 lineage continues to predominate; southern provinces show higher positivity than northern, with ages 15–59 most affected. Officials warn numbers may understate true burden due to under-testing and under-reporting. A reported case in Nanjing, Jiangsu, involving a 17-year-old student returning from Anhui, featured anosmia and limited access to antiviral therapy due to age restrictions, relying on self-paid cough medicine. Experts caution that official data reflect only the tip of the iceberg.

triage.headline_ja: 中国で複数のウイルスが同時流行、新型コロナ陽性率が数週連続で首位（動画）｜新型コロナウイルス感染症｜哨点医院｜インフルエンザウイルス
triage.triage_reason: 中国国内で季節性のCOVID-19・インフルエンザ・HMPV等の呼吸器系ウイルスが同時流行しているが、既知の病原体による季節的な増加であり、国際的拡大や渡航制限等の明確な兆候は報告されていないため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 既知の病原体（既存株Omicron NB.1.8.1、季節性インフルエンザ、HMPV、エンテロウイルス）の季節的増加であり、新規性や異常性は低い。中国国内の哨点サーベイランスデータに基づく報道で、公式データの過小評価への懸念が指摘されている。

article.articleHeadline: Can You Still Get Rabies After Vaccination?
article.articleSummary: Rabies remains one of the deadliest but preventable infections. In India, authorities plan joint reviews by health, veterinary, municipal and forest departments to investigate suspected human rabies deaths and accelerate containment amid persistent fatalities. Can rabies occur after vaccination? Yes, but it is exceptionally rare. Post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) requires three equal pillars: immediate wound washing for at least 15 minutes, rabies immunoglobulin for those not previously vaccinated, and the vaccine series to induce long‑lasting protection. True vaccine failure is uncommon and usually stems from breakdowns in care—delayed or inadequate wound cleaning, missing or incorrect vaccine doses, improper immunoglobulin infiltration, or very severe bites that hasten viral spread. Previously vaccinated individuals still need medical care after new exposures, typically needing boosters but not immunoglobulin. If bitten or scratched, wash the wound and seek prompt medical care—timing is everything.

triage.headline_ja: ワクチン接種後でも狂犬病に感染する可能性はあるか？
triage.triage_reason: 既知の風土病である狂犬病に関する一般的な啓発・解説記事であり、新規性・異常性・国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: インドにおける狂犬病サーベイランス強化とPEP（曝露後予防）の解説記事。突発的なアウトブレイクではなく、既存の風土病対策・医療情報提供が主目的。

article.articleHeadline: Kerala Reports 105 Confirmed Chikungunya Cases: 6 Symptoms In Children Parents Should Watch For
article.articleSummary: Kerala reports 105 confirmed chikungunya cases and 62 probable as of August 4, driven by intense monsoon rainfall and hot weather that boost Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus breeding, with Thiruvananthapuram accounting for the majority. The resurgence echoes prior epidemics (2006–2007, 2019–20) and underscores ongoing vector-control needs during the rainy season. Chikungunya, transmitted by infected Aedes mosquitoes, causes sudden high fever, severe joint pain, muscle aches, headache, rash, and fatigue; persistent joint pain can last weeks to months. There is no antiviral cure; management is supportive—rest, fluids, and paracetamol—guided by clinicians. Prevention hinges on eliminating standing water, covering water storage, window screens, repellents, and regular school/community mosquito-control checks. Seek medical care for fever lasting >2–3 days, severe joint pain, vomiting, dehydration, confusion, to distinguish from dengue and other infections.

triage.headline_ja: ケララ州でチクングニア熱の確定症例105件を報告：親が注意すべき子供の6つの症状
triage.triage_reason: 季節性のモンスーンに伴うチクングニア熱の増加であり、過去の流行パターンと一致する国内限定の事例。重症度や国際的拡大の兆候はないが、媒介蚊による感染拡大の可能性があるため経過観察とする。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola Nyaris 4.000 Kasus: WHO Peringatkan Kongo Masuki Fase Kritis, Ini Kunci Hentikan Wabah
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola Nearly 4,000 Cases: WHO Warns Kongo Is Entering a Critical Phase, Here Is the Key to Stopping the Outbreak
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has approached nearly 4,000 cases, with Bunia in Ituri Province a focal point of transmission. WHO and Africa CDC, after joint missions to Kampala, Uganda, and Bunia, say ending the outbreak hinges on active community engagement rather than hospitals alone. Dr. Jean Kaseya highlights that communities must receive trusted information, recognize symptoms early, and seek treatment without fear. Uganda’s outbreak was declared over on 28 July 2026, with 20 confirmed cases and 2 deaths, and all contacts monitored through the observation period. In Bunia, health workers face security instability, poor road access, displacement, and misinformation, delaying detection. WHO urges engagement of religious leaders, traditional authorities, women's groups, and youth organizations to rebuild trust, while warning that transmission persists in the DRC and cross-border surveillance remains essential.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱ほぼ4000症例：WHOがコンゴの危機的局面入りを警告、流行阻止の鍵とは
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ流行が約4000症例に達し、感染継続・国境を越えた拡大（ウガンダ）が確認されており、WHO・Africa CDCが介入する重大な公衆衛生事案であるため。
triage.notes: ウガンダでの流行は2026年7月28日に終息宣言済み（20例、死亡2例）だが、DRCでは治安不安・アクセス困難・誤情報により感染拡大が継続中。ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola v Kongu postaja najhitreje šireči se izbruh v zgodovini
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Congo is becoming the fastest-spreading outbreak in history.
article.articleSummary: As of 7 August 2026, the Democratic Republic of Congo reports 4,053 confirmed Ebola cases and 1,850 deaths across five provinces—Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, and Tshopo—with Ituri as the outbreak’s epicenter. The events involve Bundibugyo ebolavirus, for which there is no licensed vaccine or approved specific treatment. This outbreak is described as the fastest-spreading in history and the second-largest globally after the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic (over 28,000 cases). The outbreak likely began months before the 15 May declaration; a Science report suggests January or earlier, with more than 500 suspected cases identified between mid-January and 15 May, indicating true infections may be higher. Contributing factors include delayed detection, overwhelmed surveillance, ongoing eastern conflict, and lack of tailored vaccines/therapies. Access constraints due to conflict and displacement hinder response, and community transmission continues with contact tracing lagging, raising cross-border spillover risk. Keywords: outbreak, vaccination, spread, public health.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ出血熱、史上最速の拡大を見せるアウトブレイクに
triage.triage_reason: DRCで4,053例・死亡1,850人に達し、史上最速拡大かつ史上2番目の規模のエボラ流行とされ、ワクチン未承認株（ブンディブギョ株）による深刻な公衆衛生上の脅威であり、紛争地域での対応困難と越境拡散リスクも指摘されているため。

article.articleHeadline: Zahl der Ebola-Fälle im Kongo auf über 4000 gestiegen
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The number of Ebola cases in the Congo has risen to over 4,000.
article.articleSummary: 4,053 Ebola infections and 1,850 deaths have been confirmed in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, marking the second-largest and fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak on record. Five provinces are affected: Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, and Tshopo. Officials say the outbreak is likely undercounted, with the virus circulating for months before official detection on May 15. A Science paper published last month cites more than 500 cases from mid-January to May 15, suggesting earlier transmission in Ituri. Delays in detection, overwhelmed surveillance, ongoing military conflicts, and shortages of vaccines and treatments for the specific viral strain have hampered containment. The largest Ebola outbreak occurred in 2014–2016 in West Africa, with more than 28,000 cases in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A deadly outbreak is spreading rapidly! The number of cases has risen to 3,973, with a critical warning for 51 regions.
article.articleSummary: An Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has spread to 51 districts across five provinces—Haut-Uele, Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, and Tshopo. The Health Ministry reports 3,973 cases and 1,801 deaths, a case fatality rate of 45.3%; the reported contact tracing rate is updated to 753%. In the last 24 hours no new districts reported cases, while 87.1% of cases are in Ituri, the outbreak’s epicenter. Ebola virus disease, first identified in 1976 in Nzara (Sudan) and Yambuku (DRC), derives its name from the Ebola River. In Ituri there were 246 suspected cases and 65 deaths before the nationwide outbreak was declared on May 15. Officials note that the Bundibugyo Ebola variant identified in May has no approved treatment or vaccine.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Cholera outbreak in Chad kills 13 people and infects about 240 others.
article.articleSummary: Chad's cholera outbreak has caused 13 deaths and 239 infections since it was declared on 24 July, with a case-fatality rate of 5.4%. The outbreak is centered in Hadjer-Lamis governorate in northern Chad and the capital N'Djamena, where 11 of the 13 fatalities occurred this August. First deaths were recorded on 13 June, and authorities have vaccinated about 50,800 people in a response campaign to curb spread. Nationwide infections are around 239. The situation reflects a broader African pattern, with concurrent cases and deaths reported in the Central African Republic, Democratic Republic of the Congo, and Nigeria, suggesting widespread transmission on the continent. The report provides no further details on transmission sources or imported/exported cases.

article.articleHeadline: ओडिशा में गृहप्रवेश भोज और हॉस्टल का खाना खाने से हड़कंप, 90 से ज्यादा बीमार; 30 बच्चे भी शामिल - odisha food poisoning 90 plus sick after feast and hostel meal
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Panic in Odisha after housewarming feast and hostel meals; over 90 ill, including 30 children.
article.articleSummary: Two separate gastroenteritis/food-poisoning outbreaks reported in Odisha, India, on Aug 7, 2026. In Balasore district’s Jaleswar block, Khareda village hosted a housewarming feast, sickening 70+ people, including 30+ children; about 50 are in serious condition and receiving care at Jaleswar Hospital. In Mayurbhanj district’s Kapotipada block, at SSD Girls High School hostel, 275 resident girls were served fish and rice for dinner, with 19+ hospitalized at Kapotipada Hospital. Food and water samples from both sites have been sent for laboratory testing; the cause is under investigation. Health teams are conducting medical checks at the hostel and monitoring the communities. Investigations aim to determine whether illness stems from contaminated food, water, or another infection, with surveillance heightened at both locations.

article.articleHeadline: Why Chandipura virus returns every monsoon and why children face the highest risk
article.articleSummary: Chandipura virus drives seasonal outbreaks in western and central India, notably Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Andhra Pradesh, peaking during the monsoon. Recent child deaths in Gujarat underscore ongoing risk; since its 1965 identification in Maharashtra, outbreaks have recurred in monsoon seasons. Transmission is via infected sandflies; risk factors include warm, humid conditions, poor sanitation, mud walls, and livestock near homes, with children under 15 most affected due to developing immunity and outdoor exposure. Rapid progression to acute encephalitis syndrome can occur within 24-48 hours of fever, with vomiting, severe headache, drowsiness, seizures, or coma. No licensed vaccine or antiviral exists; care is supportive. A Gujarat Biotechnology Research Centre-National Institute of Virology study links early immune activation and metabolic rewiring to severe disease, naming sulfasalazine and romidepsin as potential in vitro treatments (nilotinib more toxic). Prevention emphasizes sandfly control, insecticide-treated nets, repellents, sanitation, and year-round vector surveillance.

article.articleHeadline: Study links high PM2.5 exposure to increased risk of death among tuberculosis patients during treatment
article.articleSummary: 61,925 tuberculosis patients in Delhi who started treatment between September 2022 and August 2023 showed a strong link between pre-treatment PM2.5 exposure and mortality during therapy. Risk rose with increasing pollution in the month before treatment: 3% higher mortality for 40–80 µg/m³ vs <40; and 22%, 31%, and 66% higher for 80–120, 120–160, and >160 µg/m³, respectively. Researchers linked national Nikshay TB treatment records with satellite-derived PM2.5 estimates and focused on a 30-day pre-treatment window. After adjusting for age, sex, HIV, diabetes, nutritional status, tobacco/alcohol use, treatment setting, and TB type, the association persisted, though the study remains observational and cannot prove causality. This finding highlights India’s TB burden and suggests air pollution may influence TB outcomes; authors call for reducing exposure where possible and for further research to confirm mechanisms and potential clinical implications.

triage.headline_ja: PM2.5への高濃度曝露が結核患者の治療中死亡リスク上昇と関連――研究結果

article.articleHeadline: 伊波拉疫情陰霾 民主剛果破4000例確診1850人亡 | 科學 | 伊圖里省
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Shadow over the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: more than 4,000 confirmed cases and 1,850 deaths | Science | Ituri Province
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 4,000 confirmed cases and 1,850 deaths, government data show, marking the world’s second-largest and fastest-spreading outbreak on record. The epidemic spans five provinces: Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, and Tshopo. Total infections reported reach 4,053 with 1,850 deaths. A Science study published last month indicates the virus was circulating in Ituri as early as January or earlier, with more than 500 suspected cases identified from January to May 15. Control efforts are hampered by delayed detection, overloaded surveillance, ongoing military conflict, and a lack of vaccines and treatments for this virus strain. Only the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak was larger, with over 28,000 cases in Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone.

article.articleHeadline: Κονγκό: Τα επιβεβαιωμένα κρούσματα Έμπολα ξεπέρασαν τα 4.000
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Congo: Confirmed Ebola cases surpass 4,000.
article.articleSummary: In the Democratic Republic of Congo, confirmed Ebola virus cases have surpassed 4,000 for the first time in the current outbreak, with the health institute reporting 4,053 cases and 1,850 deaths. This outbreak is the second-largest globally and the fastest-spreading on record. Experts say infections began months before the May 15 outbreak declaration, and the true toll could be higher than official counts. Cases have been documented in five provinces: Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, and Tshopo. A Science report published last month concluded the outbreak began in January or earlier in Ituri, identifying more than 500 suspected cases between mid-January and May 15. Contributing factors include delays in detection, heavy surveillance burdens, ongoing conflict, and a lack of vaccines and treatments for this Ebola strain, hindering containment. Only West Africa’s 2014–16 outbreak was larger, with over 28,000 cases in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone.

article.articleHeadline: شبح إيبولا يطارد الكونغو.. تفشٍ غير مسبوق وسلالة بلا علاج
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola specter haunts the Congo... an unprecedented outbreak and an untreatable strain.
article.articleSummary: As of August 7, 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, driven by Bundibugyo virus, has spread beyond Ituri Province into five provinces. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus warns of an unprecedented, rapid expansion with at least 3,973 laboratory-confirmed cases and more than 1,800 deaths after 80 days; recoveries at 776 and suspected cases over 220. Health authorities estimate official figures are at least fourfold undercounted due to detections outside known transmission chains. Ituri accounts for about 84% of cases and roughly 85% of the recent 99 new cases, signaling continuing concentration but risk of spread. Local operational challenges include delayed salaries for health workers in Bunia, undermining response. International action includes $242 million in US funding; Moderna beginning Phase 1 vaccine trials against the current strain, while no vaccine or treatment exists for Bundibugyo virus. Partners and African nations have raised $1.5 billion to support response and health infrastructure.

triage.triage_reason: IHR基準の複数該当（重大な公衆衛生影響、異常性、国際的拡大リスク）を満たし、致死率の高いブンディブギョ株による前例のない流行としてWHOも警鐘を鳴らしているためフルRRAへ進むべき。

article.articleHeadline: 食環署：監察地區內白紋伊蚊分布廣泛但數量不多　已加強防滅蚊行動 (16:54) - 20260807
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: FEHD: Aedes albopictus (white-striped mosquito) widely distributed in the monitored area but not numerous; has intensified mosquito-control efforts (16:54) - 2026-08-07.
article.articleSummary: Hong Kong’s Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD) reports Aedes albopictus, the white-striped mosquito, is widely distributed in the monitored area but not numerous. In the past month, FEHD conducted over 69,000 inspections, initiated 17 prosecutions for mosquito breeding, and issued 69 statutory notices to remove standing water or containers. The third phase of the citywide anti-mosquito campaign began on July 3 and runs through October 23, targeting homes, schools, construction sites, and public housing estates to eliminate breeding sites and apply ultra-low-volume mist to kill adult mosquitoes in high-risk areas. To reduce chikungunya transmission, FEHD will expand intensified control from a 20% trap-index threshold to include areas with 10–20% indices, performing risk assessments and coordinating with departments and stakeholders. Vector surveillance and targeted control will also be conducted within 250 meters of residences of chikungunya and dengue patients and at locations visited during the infection period.

triage.headline_ja: 食環署：監察地区内の白紋伊蚊は広範囲に分布するが数量は多くない　すでに防蚊・駆除活動を強化

article.articleHeadline: China's COVID-19 positivity rate shows signs of stabilization
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-08-07, China's COVID-19 activity remains moderate with signs of stabilization. For July 27–Aug 2, the positivity rate among influenza-like illness at sentinel hospitals was 22.3%, up two percentage points from the previous week and the highest among all respiratory viruses. Influenza virus positivity stood at 13.3%, followed by enterovirus at 4.1%. The China CDC said the COVID-19 uptick has moderated, with higher positivity in southern provinces than northern ones, and the 15–59 age group showing the highest rate. Influenza activity remained low overall, while other respiratory pathogens were either on a downward trend or at low levels. No case counts or deaths are provided.

triage.notes: 中国CDCによる定例的な呼吸器系サーベイランス報告。COVID-19の上昇は緩和傾向にあり、症例数・死亡者数の報告なし。

article.articleHeadline: Kasus Ebola di Kongo Tembus 4.000, Korban Meninggal Capai 1.850
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola cases in Congo surpass 4,000; death toll reaches 1,850.
article.articleSummary: 4,053 laboratory-confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), with 1,850 deaths, across five provinces: Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, and Tshopo. The outbreak, among the fastest-spreading on record, likely began in January or earlier in Ituri, with researchers identifying more than 500 suspected cases linked to Ebola between January and May 15. Detection delays, ongoing armed conflict, strained surveillance systems, and limited vaccines and treatments for the Ebola strain have hindered containment, fueling transmission. This outbreak is the second-largest globally, after the 2014-2016 West Africa outbreak (Guinea, Liberia, Sierra Leone) which had over 28,000 cases. Ebola transmits via contact with bodily fluids and through handling of corpses. Officials warn that official counts may understate true scale due to delayed detection.

article.articleSummary: As of August 7, 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has escalated to 4,053 cumulative confirmed cases with 1,850 deaths, marking it as the fastest-spreading Ebola epidemic to date. article.articleHeadline: দিল্লিতে ডেঙ্গু, এইচ১এন১-এর দাপট, আক্রান্ত প্রায় ৩০০০! কোন লক্ষণে সতর্ক হবেন?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue in Delhi, the grip of H1N1, nearly 3,000 infected! What symptoms should you watch out for?
article.articleSummary: Dengue is rising in Delhi alongside increased H1N1 (swine flu) cases during the monsoon. Delhi reports 1,389 dengue patients (1,179 residents, 210 from other states) with no deaths so far; 1,344 H1N1 cases also, again with no fatalities. Dengue is mosquito-borne; symptoms typically appear four to ten days after a bite and include sudden high fever, severe headache, retro-orbital pain, muscle and joint pains, vomiting, and rash. Red flags after fever relief include severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, breathing difficulties, bleeding from nose or gums, blood in vomit or stool, or extreme weakness. There is no specific dengue medicine; rest, fluids, and avoiding aspirin or ibuprofen. H1N1 symptoms are sudden fever, dry cough, sore throat, runny nose, headache, body aches, and fatigue. High-risk groups should seek early care; prevention emphasizes eliminating standing water, mosquito protection, hand hygiene, masking when ill, and annual vaccination.

triage.headline_ja: デリーでデング熱とH1N1が猛威、感染者約3000人！どんな症状に注意すべきか？

triage.notes: デング熱・H1N1ともに死亡例なし。モンスーン期の季節性増加であり、インド国内では毎年報告される事象。一般向け健康アドバイス記事の性質が強い。

article.articleHeadline: RDC : l'épidémie d'Ebola s'étend à deux nouvelles zones de santé, plus de 4 000 cas confirmés
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DRC: Ebola outbreak spreads to two new health zones, more than 4,000 confirmed cases.
article.articleSummary: As of 7 August 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has 4,053 laboratory-confirmed cases, 793 recoveries and 1,850 deaths (case fatality 45.7%), with 694 patients currently isolated or hospitalized. The Ituri province remains the epicenter (86.9% of cumulative cases), as two new health zones—Gombari in Haut-Uele and Bafwasende in Tshopo—are reported, bringing total zones to 53 across five provinces. Surveillance shows 1,158 alerts investigated of 1,288 signals (90.3% processed; 98.6% in North Kivu). 358 new contacts identified; national contact tracing at 77.7%. PARTNERS and EBO-PEP clinical trials continue in Ituri. Care capacity is strengthening: 17 additional recoveries (793 total), a large-capacity site opened in Tshopo with MSF support, and three ambulances in Haut-Uele. Public measures include a quarantine center, 33 PoCs, 5 PoEs, 249 Starlink kits; 3,400+ people educated; 97.2% of travelers screened; call 151 for suspected cases.

triage.triage_reason: 大規模エボラ流行(4,053例確認、致死率45.7%)が5州53保健区域に拡大しており、公衆衛生への深刻な影響と国際拡大リスクが高い。
triage.notes: MSFやEBO-PEP臨床試験等の国際支援が既に展開されており、感染拡大が継続中で新規保健区域への拡大が確認されている。致死率45.7%と非常に高い。

article.articleHeadline: Aggressiver Affe verletzt 18 Menschen in Indonesien
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Aggressive monkey injures 18 people in Indonesia.
article.articleSummary: An aggressive adult long-tailed macaque in Tembilahan, Sumatra, Indonesia, attacked people for two weeks, injuring 18 across 19 assaults, including children. The animal was trapped and later transported to Pekanbaru for blood tests and behavioral monitoring to determine if it carries disease. Some victims were vaccinated against rabies as a precaution. In response, dozens of schools in Tembilahan remained closed on Aug 7, 2026, with hundreds of students learning online; the city has not declared an all-clear yet. Officials warn a possible spillover of attacks by other monkeys. The incident highlights human–wildlife conflict driven by forest clearance for palm oil, shrinking habitats, and potential pet-keeping histories. Authorities have not yet confirmed a disease in the macaque; investigations and laboratory analyses are ongoing to assess infection status and potential public health risk.

article.articleHeadline: DR Kongo: Mehr als 4000 Menschen mit Ebola infiziert
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DR Congo: More than 4,000 people infected with Ebola.
article.articleSummary: As of 7 August 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 4,000 confirmed cases, totaling 4,053 infections and 1,850 deaths per the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention. It is the world’s second-largest outbreak and the fastest-spreading in history. Officials fear a possible viral mutation and are reviewing measures with the WHO. In response, teams will shift from traditional contact tracing to active case-finding, including door-to-door visits, since only about ten contacts per patient are currently identified, far short of the roughly 40 expected. The outbreak has persisted for more than two and a half months, centered in the conflict-affected Ituri province (mining region) and spreading to Nord-Kivu, Sud-Kivu, Haut-Uele, and Tshopo. Ebola is a viral hemorrhagic fever causing vomiting, diarrhea, organ damage, and internal bleeding.

triage.headline_ja: DRコンゴ:エボラ感染者4000人超
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRコンゴで4,000人超の感染・1,850人の死亡を記録し、史上最速の拡大ペースで複数州に拡大、ウイルス変異の懸念やWHOとの対応見直しなど公衆衛生上の深刻な影響と国際的拡大リスクが認められる。

article.articleHeadline: تفشي الكوليرا في تشاد يودي بحياة 13 شخصا
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Cholera outbreak in Chad kills 13 people.
article.articleSummary: Cholera outbreak in Chad has caused 13 deaths and about 239–240 cases since it was officially declared in July 2026 (outbreak announced July 24). By Aug 7, 11 deaths occurred in N'Djamena in August, with 239 nationwide cases and a case fatality rate of ~5.4%. The Hadjer-Lamis region in the north and the capital are most affected. Approximately 50,800 people have been vaccinated since the outbreak began. The first deaths were reported June 13. Transmission occurs via contaminated food or water; treatment is rehydration and antibiotics, but untreated cases can die within hours. Regional context includes outbreaks in Central African Republic, Democratic Republic of Congo, and Nigeria.

article.articleHeadline: تفشٍ غير مسبوق لإيبولا في الكونغو.. أكثر من 1800 وفاة
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: An unprecedented Ebola outbreak in Congo... more than 1,800 deaths.
article.articleSummary: 4053 confirmed Ebola Bundibugyo virus cases and 1,850 deaths are now reported in the Democratic Republic of Congo, the first time the outbreak has surpassed 4,000 infections. The latest update from the DRC Public Health Institute lists 4,053 cases and 1,850 fatalities, with counts above 3,900 the previous day. African CDC Director Jean Kasia said the outbreak’s intensity is unprecedented and announced plans for studies to determine whether the virus has mutated. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, during a visit to the country, warned that new infections have doubled in some hard-hit areas about three months into the outbreak, which began in May 2026. Health-system challenges include strikes by health workers over pay. The Congo outbreak is eightfold larger in cases than the comparable period of West Africa’s 2014 outbreak (Guinea, Liberia, Sierra Leone), and fatalities are more than sixfold higher at this stage.
